translationRepairs: (《Old Book of Tang》 states: Guangyi passed the civil service examination in the third year of Guangqi, was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Bureau of Merit in the Ministry of Personnel and Academician of the Hongwen Institute, and was later changed to Director of the Bureau of Provisions and Drafted Imperial Edicts.)

(《Old Book of Tang》 states: Guangyi passed the civil service examination in the third year of Guangqi, was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Bureau of Merit in the Ministry of Personnel and Academician of the Hongwen Institute, and was later changed to Director of the Bureau of Provisions, charged with drafting imperial edicts.)
膳部郎中、知制誥 names the Provisions Bureau post plus the duty of drafting edicts; the original treats 知制誥 as a coequal office titled Drafted Imperial Edicts.

After Jishu's deposition and enthronement, he traveled in the Jiangnan region to avoid calamity; Liu Yin of Lingnan treated him with deep courtesy, memorialized to appoint him as deputy commissioner, and thus he made his home beyond the mountains.)〉

After Jishu deposed and enthroned emperors, he traveled in the Jiangnan region to avoid calamity; Liu Yin of Lingnan treated him with deep courtesy, memorialized to appoint him as deputy commissioner, and thus he made his home beyond the mountains.)〉
季述廢立 means Liu Jishu deposed and installed emperors. The original possessive is ambiguous, and 'coup of deposition and enthronement' still fails to name Jishu as the agent.

Earlier there was a regulation: "When powerful families forcibly bought people's fields and houses, or framed them for confiscation and registration, and injustice was clearly obstructed, people were permitted to plead their own case."

Earlier there was a regulation: "When powerful families forcibly bought people's fields and houses, or framed them for confiscation and registration, and injustice was plainly evident, people were permitted to plead their own case."
顯有屈塞者 means a grievance plainly suffered, not that injustice was physically obstructed.

When the matter reached the Secretariat, Guangyun said to Guo Chongyao, "Fu Gong conspired in rebellion with the Shannan faction and plainly deserved punishment under the law. Our dynasty has not yet cleared his name—how can his estates be claimed?"

When the matter reached the Secretariat, Guangyun said to Guo Chongtao, "Fu Gong conspired in rebellion with the Shannan faction and plainly deserved punishment under the law. Our dynasty has not yet cleared his name—how can his estates be claimed?"
崇韜 is Chongtao; Chongyao is a false romanization of Guo Chongtao.
Chongyao privately blocked the eunuch's claim and submitted a full report to the throne.
Chongtao privately blocked the eunuch's claim and submitted a full report to the throne.
The same 崇韜 must be romanized Chongtao in this sentence.

My elder-uncle Fu Gong was framed by Zhang Jun and fell afoul of the former dynasty, when powerful ministers constrained the throne and imperial orders could not be enforced. After Wang Xingyu was executed, an edict of grace publicly cleared the record, and that edict still survives. Your Excellency is a hereditary minister of our dynasty and well versed in precedent—how can you say his name has not been cleared!

Xilang argued: "My grand-uncle Fuguang rendered great service to the throne. My elder grand-uncle Fu Gong was framed by Zhang Jun and fell afoul of the former dynasty, when powerful ministers constrained the throne and imperial orders could not be enforced. After Wang Xingyu was executed, an edict of grace publicly cleared the record, and that edict still survives. Your Excellency is a hereditary minister of our dynasty and well versed in precedent—how can you say his name has not been cleared!
伯祖 is a grandfather's elder brother (elder grand-uncle), not an elder uncle of the father's generation.
Zhang Quanyi spoke to Guo Chongyao about restoring him as chief minister, and he was soon recalled as guest of the heir apparent.
Zhang Quanyi spoke to Guo Chongtao about restoring him as chief minister, and he was soon recalled as guest of the heir apparent.
郭崇韜 is Guo Chongtao; the original Chongyao is wrong.

開府儀同三司 is the prestige title kaifu yitong sansi, not the golden-seal grand-master title 金紫光祿大夫.

Before long Jue, on grounds of old age, illness, and ear ailment, could not bear Secretariat duties; he submitted four memorials requesting release. Mingzong regretted it and only after a long time granted permission; he was then granted Grand Master with Golden Seal and Acting Left Vice Director with retirement, and was still bestowed one estate district in Zheng Prefecture.

Ren Yuan favored Li Qi, but Zheng Jue had long been at odds with Qi and Kong Xun also disliked him. Kong told An Chonghui, "Li Qi is learned enough, but he is not honest.

Ren Yuan favored Li Qi, but Zheng Jue had long been at odds with Qi and Kong Xun also disliked him. Kong told An Chonghui, "Li Qi is learned enough, but he is not honest.

Xi read the rhapsody with startled wonder, turned his shoes around to welcome him at the gate, produced Qi's 'Tuning the Mute Bell,' 'Holding Up the Sun,' and other rhapsodies, and said to Qi: "I have often lamented that in recent years literati rhapsodies, after several lines one still has not seen the rhapsody's topic. Your lordship from the opening lines reveals the topic, and the pairing is classically splendid—ah!
余嘗患 is Li Xi speaking of himself, not 臣; 偶屬典麗 is parallel diction, not 'occasional' elegance.

At the beginning of the Tianfu era he entered the Broad Learning and Eminent Rhetoric examination and placed in the fourth rank. He was appointed captain of Wei Gong County, then recruited as a transport circuit inspector, and later promoted to left remonstrating official and palace remonstrating censor.

He was appointed captain of Wugong County, then recruited as a transport circuit inspector, and later promoted to left remonstrating official and palace remonstrating censor.
武功縣 is the county Wugong, not a personal name Wei Gong.

In Zhenming and Longde, successively Minister of War, Rites, and Personnel; ordered with Feng Xijia, Zhang Chong, and Xi Yinxiang jointly to compile 《Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu of Liang》 thirty volumes; promoted to Censor-in-Chief, repeatedly raised to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

In Zhenming and Longde, successively vice minister of War, Rites, and Personnel; ordered with Feng Xijia, Zhang Chong, and Xi Yinxiang jointly to compile 《Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu of Liang》 thirty volumes; promoted to Censor-in-Chief, repeatedly raised to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
兵、禮、吏侍郎 are vice-minister posts; 侍郎 is not minister.

Once, while Qi was handling personnel matters during the examination season, he changed the provisional title 'acting' to 'holding office' in an appointment. Qing reported this, and the Liang emperor was furious and was about to banish him to the remote frontier. Zhao Yan and others intervened on his behalf. He was removed as chief minister and made crown prince junior tutor.

Once, while Qi was issuing an appointment with a probationary title, he changed the designation from 'acting' to 'holding the post.' Qing reported this, and the Liang emperor was furious and was about to banish him to the remote frontier. Zhao Yan and others intervened on his behalf. He was removed as chief minister and made crown prince junior tutor.

The source describes changing the formal appointment grade from 'acting' to 'holding the post,' not personnel work during an examination season. The revision preserves that distinction without inserting Chinese characters into the English text.

In Later Han, during the reign of Emperor An, when flood and drought left stores insufficient, the Three Excellencies memorialized that wealthy men who contributed grain might receive the rank of marquis within the passes or various honorary posts down to the level of the Three Excellencies.

In Later Han, during the reign of Emperor An, when flood and drought left stores insufficient, the Three Excellencies memorialized that wealthy men who contributed grain might receive the rank of marquis within the passes or honorary posts of the Three Excellencies and ministers and below.
公卿以下散官 are honorary posts of the Three Excellencies and ministers and below, not a scale ending at the Three Excellencies.
He also once memorialized at imperial order to compose the spirit-way stele text for Huo Yanwei.
He also once, by imperial command, composed the spirit-way stele text for Huo Yanwei.
The chapter writes 秦敕, a graphic variant of 奉敕: Qi received an imperial command to compose the stele, he did not memorialize for leave to do so.
He also once memorialized at imperial order to compose the spirit-way stele text for Huo Yanwei.
He also once received imperial command to compose the spirit-way stele text for Huo Yanwei.
The literal repeats the false 'memorialized'; standard editions read 奉敕, composition by imperial command.
He was the grandson of the former official Xiang and the son of Lin, governor of Jingzhao.
He was the grandson of the former chief minister Fang and the son of Lin, governor of Jingzhao.
故相仿 is former chief minister Fang (蕭仿), not a generic official named Xiang.

Qing was quick-witted and skilled at prose. In the reign of Emperor Zhaozong he passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as transport circuit inspector, doctor of the Grand Ceremonies, and right supplementing remonstrator.

Qing was quick-witted and skilled at prose. In the reign of Emperor Zhaozong he passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as inspector of the Census Bureau, doctor of the Grand Ceremonies, and right supplementing remonstrator.
度支巡官 is a fiscal/census inspectorate post, not a transport-circuit appointment.

Every provincial ministry said there was no precedent, but Zhang Jun bent the rules to carry it out. His order was extremely urgent, and the clerks were terrified.

Earlier, when Zhang Jun left the Secretariat to become right vice director, Gao Shao, a judge on the staff of the Founder of Liang, had the Founder's yin request an initial appointment for a son. All the capital ministries and courts said there was no precedent, but Zhang Jun bent the rules to carry it out. His order was extremely urgent, and the clerks were terrified.

When Emperor Zhuangzong took Bian, Qing was demoted to registrar of Deng Prefecture and transferred by commutation of place to vice prefect of Pu Prefecture.
量移 is commutation of an exile posting to a nearer place, not a merely prompt transfer.
